preamble: The alveolar trill [r] can be replaced by a voiceless uvular fricative [χ], shifting the place of articulation back to the uvula and losing both trilling and voicing. The change is typical of the 'strong r' of Portuguese, where the classical trill [r] has given way to uvular [ʁ]/[χ] in Europe and to voiceless back fricatives in Brazil. In Germanic languages that have adopted uvular r, the rhotic is likewise devoiced to [χ] after voiceless obstruents (German) or in codas (Dutch of Nijmegen and Flemish cities).

examples.note: The 'strong r' (word-initial and 'rr'), originally an alveolar trill still common in African and some European varieties, is typically uvular [ʁ] or [χ] in Europe and a voiceless velar, uvular or glottal fricative in most Brazilian dialects.
Uvular /r/ is devoiced after voiceless plosives and fricatives; in Standard Austrian German the uvular rhotic varies freely between voiced [ʁ] and voiceless [χ].

Sebregts' survey of Dutch rhotics finds voiceless uvular fricative [χ] among the common coda realizations of /r/ in Nijmegen and frequent in codas in Ghent, Hasselt and Brussels; [χ] also occurs in onsets in The Hague and Leiden.
